anomalies.impact: The ATO valve MOSFET is a 30 V‑rated part switching a 24 V inductive solenoid. With only ~6 V of Vds headroom, the SMBJ28A input clamp (≈45 V surge clamp) or supply overshoot can exceed the AO3400A's Vds rating and destroy the valve switch; the 8‑DFN footprint called out for the AON6407 is also not what is drawn.

anomalies.obs: On sheet 1 the TF‑Luna LiDAR PR4 is wired: VCC→+5 V, SCL→NET0007, SDA→NET0006 (the main non‑isolated I2C bus, the same nets carried by the R42/R54 2.2 kΩ pull‑ups and the ESP32 IO4/IO5), through header H12.
anomalies.exp: Spec §4.3/§6 state the LiDAR is schematic documentation only: "the r2 netlist shows PR1 with on_board: no ... and all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net in this design."

anomalies.impact: An I2C device the intended design deliberately left unconnected is now bridged onto the main I2C bus; if a TF‑Luna is plugged into H12 it appears as an unmanaged slave and adds bus loading/capacitance, contrary to the architecture (water level is meant to be sensed by the float switches, not the LiDAR).

parsed.summary: The drawing deviates from the intended r2 design in two places: the ATO‑valve low‑side switch is built with a 30 V AO3400A instead of the spec‑mandated AON6407 (insufficient Vds headroom on a 24 V inductive load), and the TF‑Luna LiDAR, which the spec says must be left unwired with free pins, is in fact tied onto the main I2C bus via H12.
